name: Express
summary: A minimal Node.js web framework that represents an application as a configurable middleware and route pipeline over Node HTTP request and response objects.

features.name: Ordered middleware pipeline
features.description: Applications register middleware with app.use; the application delegates request handling to its router, which invokes handlers in registration and route-matching order and passes control through next callbacks.
benefits: Small request concerns can be composed incrementally
Mounted applications and middleware can share the same dispatch boundary
costs: Ordering and error propagation are operational correctness concerns
A long or branching chain increases lifecycle reasoning cost

features.name: Route and method dispatch
features.description: Express proxies HTTP verb methods and route creation to a Router; each route has an isolated middleware stack, while app.all applies handlers across methods.
benefits: Routes are explicit and can be grouped by path and method
costs: Matching semantics and route order affect which handler executes
The framework delegates substantial behavior to the separate router module

features.name: Node HTTP request/response adapter
features.description: On dispatch, Express links req and res, installs Express request and response prototypes, initializes res.locals, and forwards the pair to the router; helpers add parsing, content negotiation, and response formatting.
benefits: Preserves Node HTTP compatibility while providing framework helpers
Allows application-specific request and response behavior through prototype delegation
costs: Prototype mutation and shared helper state require careful integration
Convenience helpers do not replace HTTP lifecycle and stream constraints

features.name: Mounted application and view boundaries
features.description: An Express application can be mounted as middleware under a path, restoring parent request and response prototypes after the child handles the request; configured view engines provide a rendering boundary.
benefits: Separates route dispatch from optional template rendering
costs: Nested app state and prototype restoration add boundary complexity
View engines introduce external rendering and caching contracts

mathematical_views.question: How does a request traverse middleware, route matching, terminal handlers, and error handlers?
assumptions: Each middleware is modeled as a partial function from request state to next/response/error
Registration order and path/method predicates determine enabled transitions
The view abstracts Node event-loop scheduling and stream backpressure

mathematical_views.question: How do routers, paths, methods, and mounted subapplications determine handler selection?
assumptions: Router layers are graph nodes with path and method labels
A request follows matching layers until a terminal response or error
The separate router package's complete matching algorithm is outside this card's fixed Express source

mathematical_views.question: Which Express request/response operations refine the underlying Node HTTP objects without changing the transport boundary?
assumptions: Node request and response objects are the base interface
Express prototypes and helpers are an observationally richer interface
This is a candidate refinement view, not a proof of behavioral equivalence for every helper

costs: Correctness depends on order, next usage, and error paths
Route matching and registration order remain coupled

benefits: Convenient framework API over Node HTTP
costs: Prototype and stream integration constraints remain visible
Nested state and external view-engine contracts add complexity
